annotations.hypothesis: Root: p = sigmoid(z), z = -0.487 + LINEAR CORE + 0.136*ischaemia_gate + 0.252*bp_offset_gate - 0.118*ischaemia_damping_thal6 + 0.729*lvh_without_exercise_angina + 0.048*high_fasting_sugar. LINEAR CORE (17 direct input->output edges, z-scored inputs): ca +1.473, sex:0 -1.062, slope:1 -0.921, chol +0.522, trestbps +0.498, cp:1 -0.489, exang:1 +0.471, cp:3 -0.444, thal:3 -0.423, thal:6 -0.413, slope:3 -0.370, cp:4 +0.357, fbs:0 +0.264, thalach -0.226, restecg:0 -0.159, exang:0 +0.136, age +0.126. Five inputs are unconnected (sex:1, cp:2, restecg:1, slope:2, thal:7; zero-effect entries of this root). Oldpeak, thal:4, restecg:2 and fbs:1 have no direct edge and act only through the children. COMPOSITION: additive readouts, with a serial fan-out inside. ischaemia_gate (oldpeak above a resting-ECG-dependent threshold) is read out directly and also feeds bp_offset_gate (the ischaemia score minus a resting-BP offset, the largest nonlinear readout) and ischaemia_damping_thal6 (a near-linear term that takes back part of the ischaemia score and adds a fixed-defect term); identity nodes identity_290 and identity_1416 carry those two links so each gate is its own leaf. Two independent indicators add to z: lvh_without_exercise_angina (+0.236 for LVH on the resting ECG without exercise angina) and high_fasting_sugar (+0.074, negligible). EVIDENCE (train, n=242): full model AUC 0.9389, acc 0.880 (compute_performance). Linear core alone AUC 0.933; logit SD 3.19 (core) vs 0.57 (all hidden readouts). Removing the ischaemia gate with its downstream effects gives 0.932; readout-only ablations: ischaemia 0.938, BP 0.933, damping 0.938, LVH 0.939, fbs 0.939. Treating all five ReLUs as identities gives 0.917 (the gating matters); one least-squares linear fit of all hidden readouts on their inputs gives 0.938 (R2 0.84); an L2 logistic regression on all 26 inputs gives 0.936. Mean |SHAP| (train, all 242): ca 0.145, sex:0 0.109, slope:1 0.108, thal:3 0.050, oldpeak 0.047, cp:3 0.045, exang:1 0.044, chol 0.043. Interpretation: close to logistic regression plus one ischaemia correction: ST depression raises risk only above a threshold that is lower with a normal resting ECG, more steeply when resting BP is low; LVH without exercise angina adds a little. Counter-directional signs reported, not explained: restecg:0 positive in the ischaemia gate, trestbps negative in the BP gate, thal:6 (fixed defect) negative directly, fbs:0 +0.26 directly. Same core design as the 10-seed heart-s5 record (key 9330) and the sibling cluster lead heart-s5-c1 (ischaemia gate -> resting-BP gate), with a damping node, an LVH indicator and a fasting-sugar indicator instead of c1's age gate.

sentences.label: Lowering the risk
sentences.text: These add up independently, and these lower the risk: being a woman takes a typical patient's predicted risk from about 20% to about 3%; through this sum alone typical angina lowers it to about 2%, non-anginal chest pain to about 4%, fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL to about 10% and atypical angina to about 11%; and a higher maximum heart rate lowers it steadily, from about 26% at 118 to about 16% at 175 beats per minute.

sentences.label: Raising the risk
sentences.text: Each extra vessel coloured by fluoroscopy adds about the same, from about 20% at 0 to about 87% at 2 vessels, flattening out near the top because the predicted risk cannot go much higher; a flat rather than upsloping ST segment raises it to about 61%, higher cholesterol raises it steadily from about 13% at 193 mg/dL to about 34% at 308 mg/dL, and older age raises it steadily from about 17% at 42 to about 22% at 66 years.

Through this sum alone, higher resting blood pressure raises it steadily, from about 12% at 110 mm Hg to about 33% at 155 mm Hg, a thallium result other than a normal scan or a fixed defect raises it to about 36%, chest pain brought on by exercise raises it to about 33%, and a resting ECG other than normal raises it to about 25%; all four also act through the parts below.

sentences.label: Rare results
sentences.text: Some rarer results also count (the model has little data on this, n = 15 to 17): through this sum alone a fixed defect on the thallium scan lowers the risk to about 9%, and a downsloping ST segment raises it to about 27%.

This part reads ST depression on exercise, the resting ECG and the thallium scan, and acts on 109 of 242 training patients, 65 of whom had heart disease; for the typical patient it acts on, the predicted risk is about 76% without it and about 89% with it.

Through it, more ST depression adds to the predicted risk only once it rises above about 1.3 mm (between 0.4 and 1.3 mm for different patients), rising in an uneven way: for a typical patient from about 16% at 0 mm to about 50% at 2.8 mm.
ST depression counts more with a normal resting ECG (from about 16% to about 50%) than with any other resting ECG (from about 25% to about 48%), in an uneven way.
Through it, a resting ECG other than normal lowers a typical patient's risk from about 20% to about 16%, and a thallium result coded 4 shuts the signal (the model has little data on this, n = 2).

This part reads that signal together with resting blood pressure, chest pain on exercise and chest pain type, and acts on 145 of 242 training patients, 73 of whom had heart disease; for the typical patient it acts on, the predicted risk is about 51% without it and about 68% with it.

Through it, higher resting blood pressure lowers the risk up to about 125 mm Hg (between 122 and 165 mm Hg for different patients), then no further, in an uneven way: for a typical patient from about 23% at 110 mm Hg to about 17% at 155 mm Hg.
Through it, chest pain on exercise lowers a typical patient's risk from about 20% to about 18%, and non-anginal chest pain to about 19%.

This part reads the same signal and the thallium scan, and acts on 234 of 242 training patients, 102 of whom had heart disease; for the typical patient it acts on, the predicted risk is about 24% without it and about 20% with it.
Through it, a fixed defect on the thallium scan raises a typical patient's risk from about 20% to about 23% (the model has little data on this, n = 15).

This part acts on 74 of 242 training patients, nearly all with left ventricular hypertrophy on the resting ECG and no chest pain on exercise, 30 of whom had heart disease; for the typical patient it acts on, the predicted risk is about 25% without it and about 30% with it.

Through it, left ventricular hypertrophy raises a typical patient's risk from about 20% to about 24%, and for the typical patient it acts on, chest pain on exercise lowers it from about 30% to about 25%.
Across the model, chest pain on exercise raises a typical patient's risk from about 20% to about 31% without left ventricular hypertrophy, and from about 25% to about 35% with it.

This part acts on 33 of 242 training patients, nearly all with fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL, 15 of whom had heart disease; for the typical patient it acts on, the predicted risk is about 24% without it and about 25% with it.
It barely changes the predictions, by at most 2 percentage points.

Changing one input at a time across the whole model, more ST depression raises a typical patient's predicted risk in an uneven way, from about 16% at 0 mm to about 50% at 2.8 mm, and higher resting blood pressure raises it in an uneven way, from about 15% at 110 mm Hg to about 28% at 155 mm Hg; through the sum alone it rises steadily, from about 12% to about 33%.

analysis.note: The ischaemia gate 204 fans out to the output, to the BP gate 290 and to the damping node 1416, each read out directly into the logit; 1611 (LVH without exercise angina) and 3884 (high fasting sugar) are independent indicators. 'Readout only' removes a node's direct edge to the output and leaves downstream nodes unchanged; 'node with downstream' replaces the node's activation (zero or train mean) and propagates. Linear replacement = the node's ReLU replaced by the least-squares affine fit of its activation on its own inputs, propagated. Removing the ischaemia gate with its downstream effects takes the model just below the linear-core level (0.932 vs 0.933); all hidden readouts together add +0.006 train AUC. Treating every ReLU as identity drops AUC to 0.917, so the gating (not the extra terms) is what the hidden nodes contribute.
